cohort: The study included 109 pregnant women with sickle cell disease (51 with HbSS and 44 with HbSC) in the UK.
finding: The study confirmed a high rate of maternal and fetal complications in mothers with SCD, with women with HbSS experiencing more acute pain, blood transfusions, UTIs, critical care admissions, preterm delivery, and babies with reduced birth weight compared to HbSC.
cross-section timing: Data collected between 1 February 2010 and 31 January 2011
